title: South Korea Launches Nationwide Open Quantum Testbed Expansion Led by KT and SK Broadband - Quantum Computing Report
gist: South Korea's MSIT and NIA kicked off a three-year (2026-2028) Open Quantum Testbed expansion, with 7.4 billion won in first-year funding split between government and private money, extending quantum communications from the Seoul-Pangyo-Daejeon corridor nationwide by 2028. KT runs the Commercial Hub (multi-vendor terrestrial QKD) and Future Hub (free-space QKD from 4.8 km to 15 km, entanglement distribution), while SK Broadband runs the International Hub pairing QKD with PQC to Singapore, Poland and Bulgaria.

insights.claim: South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT and the National Information Society Agency began the three-year (2026-2028) Open Quantum Testbed Advancement and Expansion Project to extend quantum communications beyond the Seoul-Pangyo-Daejeon corridor into a nationwide infrastructure by 2028.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Government-backed national QKD buildout creates demand for domestic quantum-comms vendors.
insights.locator: South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT

insights.claim: First-year investment is 7.4 billion won (~$5.6M), made up of 3.75 billion won in government funding and 3.65 billion won from private-sector contributions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Funding is small in absolute terms; strategic signal outweighs revenue impact for KT and SK Broadband.
insights.quote: initial first-year investment of 7.4 billion won (~$5.6 million USD)

insights.claim: KT Corporation (KRX: 030200) was selected to build and operate both the Commercial Hub (Section A) and Future Hub (Section C), while SK Broadband leads the International/Overseas Hub (Section B).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: KT wins two of three sections, reinforcing its position as Korea's lead quantum-comms operator.

themes.theme: Section A: KT terrestrial multi-vendor QKD

insights.claim: KT's Section A rollout centers on Daejeon and extends to Daegu in 2026, Gwangju and Busan in 2027, and Seoul to Gangwon (Chuncheon) in 2028.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Dated rollout schedule offers milestones to monitor KT's execution.

insights.claim: A main goal of Section A is an open multi-vendor verification framework where domestic optical-network makers can test QKD appliances, key management systems and encryptors for interoperability, with live commercial pilots in healthcare and finance.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Interoperability testbeds lower barriers for Korean QKD equipment makers to commercialize.
insights.locator: In Section A, KT will center

themes.theme: Section B: SK Broadband hybrid QKD-PQC international links

insights.claim: SK Broadband will demonstrate a hybrid defense-in-depth design in which QKD secures domestic and localized overseas segments while post-quantum cryptography protects long-distance transit links to partner testbeds in Singapore, Poland and Bulgaria.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid QKD+PQC is emerging as the practical model for long-haul; favors PQC software vendors for cross-border links.
insights.quote: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms will be applied across long-distance transit links
insights.locator: For cross-border links in Section B

insights.claim: Section B's cross-border links are intended to support secure scientific data transmission and Urban Air Mobility communication security.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: UAM is cited as an early use case; niche near-term demand.
insights.locator: For cross-border links in Section B

themes.theme: Section C: free-space QKD and entanglement distribution

insights.claim: KT's Future Hub aims to triple free-space wireless QKD range from 4.8 km to 15 km using modular transceivers and adaptive optics to counteract atmospheric turbulence.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Free-space reach is a prerequisite for satellite QKD; watch for demonstrated 15 km results.
insights.quote: aiming to triple transmission range from 4.8 km to 15 km using modular transceivers and adaptive optics
insights.locator: In Section C, KT is advancing

insights.claim: Section C also serves as a proving ground for multi-point quantum entanglement distribution, building the routing layers needed for distributed quantum computing clusters and future quantum satellite uplinks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Early groundwork for a quantum internet; long-dated optionality for KT.
insights.locator: In Section C, KT is advancing
